source_reviews.date_assessment: Single XML day 20 September 1837; Darwin-authored outgoing letter to A. Y. Spearman.
source_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin voice throughout. It acknowledges the Treasury's 31 August grant, proposes Smith, Elder and Company as publisher, and encloses the plan and supporting documents for Treasury consideration.

evidence.quote: acknowledge the receipt of your letter of August 31st
the plan suggested by Smith, Elder and Cony appears to me very much the best
place this and the accompanying documents for their Lordships consideration at an early day

source_reviews.date_assessment: Single XML day 11 October 1837; preserved as a Treasury out-letter with no date uncertainty.
source_reviews.attribution_assessment: The surviving institutional response is authored/signed by Francis Thornhill Baring, not A. Y. Spearman. Baring reports the Lords Commissioners' command to Darwin and responds to Darwin's 20 September plan.

evidence.quote: [Francis Thornhill Baring] 11 October 1837
Having laid before the Lords &c your Letter of 20th. ulto. & the accompanying Plan
my Lords will be glad to hear that you are proceeding in the Work in the manner therein suggested

source_reviews.date_assessment: Single XML day 16 February 1838; Darwin-authored outgoing letter to A. Y. Spearman.
source_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin voice throughout. He invokes the September plan and the October approval, files Smith and Elder's first-part account, notes that a copy went to the Chancellor of the Exchequer, and asks Treasury how the publisher should draw.

evidence.quote: the plan proposed in the documents accompanying my letter September 20th 1837
which received (October 11th) the entire approval of the Lords Commissioner
enclose the account of Mrss. Smith and Elder for the first part of the work

source_reviews.date_assessment: Single XML day 24 May 1838; Darwin-authored outgoing letter to Charles Wood.
source_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin voice in the surviving request and address block. He asks the Admiralty for permission to engrave a published chart of Ascension Island for his scientific account of its geology.

evidence.quote: beg the permission of the Lords of the Admiralty
a copy of the published Admiralty chart of that island, engraved
To | Charles Wood Esqr

source_reviews.date_assessment: XML day 26 May 1838; header retains editorial brackets around the year.
source_reviews.attribution_assessment: Francis Beaufort's institutional reply to Darwin. It reports an Admiralty command and gives practical instructions for taking a transfer proof; it is not Darwin voice and does not make Beaufort interchangeable with Charles Wood.

evidence.quote: From Francis Beaufort 26 May [1838]
supply you with a copy of our plan of Ascension Id. in order to its being engraved
send your lithographer to this office with the proper ink for taking a transfer proof

proposed_links.reason: 381A explicitly states that Baring laid before the Lords Commissioners Darwin's 20 September letter and accompanying plan, then communicates their entire approval. This is a direct institutional administrative response, not merely evidence that Treasury knew of Darwin's project.
proposed_links.response_scope: Whole surviving body of 381A; it is a two-paragraph administrative response to 378A's plan and request.

evidence.quote: the accompanying documents for their Lordships consideration
Having laid before the Lords &c your Letter of 20th. ulto. & the accompanying Plan
their entire approval of the proposals contained therein

caveats: 381A is Baring's institutional communication on behalf of the Treasury Lords; Baring must not be aliased to Spearman, the addressee of 378A.

proposed_links.reason: 402A explicitly cites the October 11 approval communicated in 381A while submitting the first Smith and Elder account and asking how the publisher should draw on Treasury. It is a direct administrative follow-up to the approval, with 378A retained as the originating plan rather than duplicated as a second reply edge.
proposed_links.response_scope: Whole surviving body of 402A; paragraph 1 carries the explicit approval reference and account filing, paragraphs 2-4 complete the administrative request.

evidence.quote: my Lords will be glad to hear that you are proceeding in the Work
which received (October 11th) the entire approval
communicate to me, according to what form Mrss. Smith and Elder ought to draw on the Treasury

caveats: 402A is addressed to Spearman, while 381A is Baring's signed Treasury response to Darwin; the chain is institutional and must preserve both representatives' identities.

proposed_links.reason: 415B supplies the exact Ascension chart copy and transfer-proof procedure requested in 415A two days earlier. This is a reverse institutional administrative reply to Darwin's request, not a Darwin prompt or a knowledge-only link.
proposed_links.response_scope: Whole surviving body of 415B; paragraph 1 fulfills the chart request and paragraph 2 gives the reproduction procedure.

evidence.quote: a copy of the published Admiralty chart of that island, engraved
supply you with a copy of our plan of Ascension Id. in order to its being engraved
reproduce as many impressions as you may think fit

caveats: 415A is Darwin to Charles Wood; 415B is Francis Beaufort to Darwin. The distinct officials are linked by the request and fulfillment, not by aliasing their identities.

institutional_identity.DCP-LETT-381A: Francis Thornhill Baring to Darwin, communicating the Lords Commissioners' approval
institutional_identity.DCP-LETT-415A: Darwin to Charles Wood, requesting Admiralty chart permission
institutional_identity.DCP-LETT-415B: Francis Beaufort to Darwin, supplying the Ascension plan and transfer-proof instructions
institutional_identity.warning: Baring and Spearman are distinct institutional representatives. The 381A-to-378A edge is supported by explicit content, but not because the named people are interchangeable.

excluded_duplicate.reason: The earlier Treasury grant context is acknowledged in 378A and is already accepted; no duplicate link is proposed here.

issues: These are direct administrative follow-ups concerning Treasury support for Zoology of the Voyage of H.M.S. Beagle, not knowledge-only topic links.
The chain crosses representatives: Darwin writes Spearman, Baring communicates the Lords Commissioners' decision, and Darwin writes Spearman again. Preserve Baring versus Spearman attribution.
The enclosed Smith and Elder statements/accounts are referenced as administrative enclosures; their existence does not alter the direct body-level links or supply additional Darwin voice.
